_comment: The 'Mangal' — a tank wearing a shed. Authored from reference photographs at
incoming/factions/russian-federation/units/mangal/ (gitignored: third-party rights, and
they inform PARAMETERS only — silhouette, proportion, palette — never pixels).
The side-profile still is the frame that matters. Everything about this vehicle is one
shape: a pitched-roof carapace covering the whole hull, overhanging forward, with the
barrel emerging from under its front edge. That is why `ridge` had to exist — `taper`
narrows both non-axis dimensions equally and so makes a pyramid where a roof is wanted.
+X is FORWARD, matching how retail vehicles are laid out: AVLeopard's long axis is X.
Z is up, and z = 0 is the ground, so a part's `at` is the CENTRE of its box.
THREE THINGS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT GEOMETRY. The cope-cage grid and the camo netting are
wire and mesh; at a 245-triangle peer budget (AVLeopard) they are a texture with alpha,
not vertices. Modelling them would spend the entire model on something invisible at RTS
camera distance.
AND NEITHER ARE THE ROAD WHEELS, which is the lesson this recipe cost. They were authored
first — six cylinders arrayed and mirrored, 240 of 436 triangles, 55% of the model — and
the render showed exactly none of them: a wheel 3 units thick at y = 8.5 sits INSIDE a
track box 5 units thick at the same y. Invisible, and more than half the budget. Retail
reaches the same conclusion by a different route: AVLeopard carries flat TREADSL01 /
TREADSR01 strips and puts the links and wheels in a scrolling texture. So the wheels go
to the texture and the triangles go to the bow, where they can be seen.
AND THE CARAPACE IS NOT A TURRET. It is welded on and cannot rotate. That is a real trait
— a forward-only firing arc the sim can express — rather than a modelling shortcut, and
the part names below say so: there is no TURRET for an INI Draw module to bind.
name: MANGAL

parts._: Track runs. Boxes, not modelled links: the links AND the road wheels live in the
parts.__: texture, which is what AVLeopard's flat TREADSL01/TREADSR01 strips do. Mirrored
parts.___: across Y so one authored run gives both sides.
parts.name: TRACKS

parts._: The hull proper, mostly swallowed by the carapace — but it has to exist, or the
parts.__: shed floats between two track runs the moment the camera drops.
parts.name: HULL

parts._: THE CARAPACE — the entire silhouette. The ridge runs along X so the roof slopes
parts.__: to both flanks, and ridgeWidth 0.18 leaves the narrow flat the reference shows
parts.___: instead of a knife edge. Lowered to sit ON the track line: the first attempt put
parts.____: it 13 units tall starting at z=13.5, which rendered as a tent on skis. The
parts._____: reference is LONG and LOW — roughly 3:1 length to height, not 2:1.
parts.name: CARAPACE

parts._: Bow plate. A wedge under the carapace's front overhang, where the reference has
parts.__: the sloped glacis and the mine plough mount. This is where the wheels' triangles
parts.___: went, and unlike the wheels it is visible from every angle the game uses.
parts.name: BOW

parts._: Gun. Emerges from under the carapace lip rather than from a turret face, and low
parts.__: — in the reference it clears the bow by very little. rot [0,90,0] swings the
parts.___: cylinder's Z onto X so it points forward.
parts.name: BARREL
